name: The Wolfgang Press
label: 4AD
lede: Three refugees from 4AD's earliest bands made what John Peel called the most morose record he'd ever heard, then discovered De La Soul, scored a US hit with A Girl Like You and watched Tom Jones cover it.

eras.title: Before the Press, 4AD's first serious band
eras.text: Michael Allen and Mark Cox came up through Rema-Rema and Mass, two of the first acts on Ivo Watts-Russell's new label. Andrew Gray was in In Camera, another early 4AD band. The Wolfgang Press was built entirely from 4AD's own spare parts.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press · The Quietus
years.h: Rema-Rema's demo makes Ivo take his label seriously
years.p: Allen and schoolmate Gary Asquith's band, with Cox and Marco Pirroni, issues one record: the Wheel in the Roses EP, 4AD BAD 5. Pirroni leaves for Adam and the Ants and the band folds.
years.xp:
Ivo Watts-Russell said hearing Rema-Rema's demo was "the first point I knew that we were actually doing something serious" with 4AD. The Quietus calls them the first band to release a record bearing the 4AD logo.

Pirroni later said Adam Ant didn't headhunt him: he says he'd already left Rema-Rema when the call came.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Rema-Rema regroups as Mass
years.p: Allen, Cox, Asquith and Danny Briottet put out You and I on 4AD, then the album Labour of Love in May 1981. Mass splits that year; Asquith and Briottet later form [[Renegade Soundwave|5e074654-aad2-4944-bce6-3aa1d16bb2d2]].

eras.title: Gloom, on purpose
eras.text: Allen and Cox kept writing after Mass, and Ivo told them to make an album. The early Wolfgang Press was slow, dark and hard going, and proud of it; Cocteau Twin Robin Guthrie produced the EPs that loosened it up.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Two songs written in Cox's bedroom become an album deal
years.p: Allen and Cox take Ivo the two tracks they'd written in Cox's bedroom. He suggests they make an album. The name, Allen says, was picked to be meaningless.
years.xp: Spin printed the band's own story that the name came from a machine Mozart tried, and failed, to invent for typing out his music. No such device is known. Other sources tie it to the German actor Wolfgang Preiss. Allen has said the point was to be "meaningless and open to interpretation."

years.big: "The most consciously morose record I've ever heard."
q: The most consciously morose record I've ever heard.
years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: The Burden of Mules arrives
years.p: John Peel's verdict on the debut. Andrew Gray plays guitar and percussion as a guest, with Richard Thomas of Dif Juz.
years.xp:
Trouser Press heard "an angry, intense slab of post-punk gloom"; ZigZag called it an emphatic statement. The band's own 2001 retrospective, Everything Is Beautiful, leaves it out entirely.

Forty-one years later they'd come back to exactly this sound for A 2nd Shape.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press · Louder Than War
years.h: Andrew Gray joins, and Robin Guthrie takes the controls
years.p: Gray, ex-In Camera, becomes the third member. Scarecrow is the first of three EPs produced by Cocteau Twins' Guthrie, and a lighter, leaner thing than the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Water and Sweatbox follow, then get a joke title
years.p: The two 1985 EPs, from torch songs to what AllMusic called deconstructionist pop, are collected with Scarecrow as The Legendary Wolfgang Press and Other Tall Stories.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Standing Up Straight adds strings and clatter
years.p: Produced with [[John Fryer|17375716-41de-49a9-8b9c-64c71bb14742]], who'd worked on [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]] and [[This Mortal Coil|60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6]]. 4AD's own profile called it industrial and classical tropes in one blend.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: The Big Sex EP previews the turn
years.p: Recorded in December 1986, the four-track EP points straight at what comes next: grooves under the gloom.

eras.title: Flood, then De La Soul
eras.text: Producer Flood tightened the band up on Bird Wood Cage, and funk started leaking in. Then a hip-hop record convinced three post-punks that music could be fun, and the result went to No. 2 on the American alternative chart.

years.cap: Ticket for Pixies with the Wolfgang Press supporting, The Studio, Bristol
years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: "We came of age with Bird Wood Cage," says Allen
years.p: Wah-wah guitar, dub, women singing backup, and Flood helping the band sound coherent. Allen has called it the Wolfgang Press record he's proudest of.
years.xp: AllMusic saw it as the pivot where dance and funk began to take over. King of Soul, Kansas and Raintime came out as singles; Allen admits it sold modestly.

years.src: Louder Than War · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Kennedy masks for the Kansas video
years.p: The Kansas single gets one of the band's signature videos, with John and Jackie Kennedy masks; they'd come back for Going South.

years.cap: Mick Allen in a US press photo
years.src: Seb Chan · The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: De La Soul turns the Wolfgang Press into a groove band
years.p: Queer runs on samples, with Dif Juz's Richie Thomas on drums and [[Throwing Muses|b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8]] bassist [[Leslie Langston|5d9bb2c3-a707-4ef7-a7a3-8fb74776b255]]. Time samples [[Pink Floyd|83d91898-7763-47d7-b03b-b92132375c47]]; the next single is Randy Newman's Mama Told Me Not to Come.
years.xp:
The spark was 3 Feet High and Rising. Allen said it was where they "rediscovered that music could indeed be fun," and the Quietus quotes him wanting the same joy and looseness.

Early vinyl copies came with Sucker, a 12-inch of remixes by Martyn Young of [[Colourbox|6746c384-b67b-4eb7-a986-e2b6f4140cee]].

years.cap: Michael Allen, Mark Cox and Andrew Gray
years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
yt: A Girl Like You, official video
years.h: A Girl Like You hits No. 2 on the US modern rock chart
years.p: Released in May with Warner Bros. in America, the single climbs to No. 2 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks. To get Queer out in the US, the band had to rerecord and remix around uncleared samples.

eras.title: Tom Jones on line one
eras.text: The hit brought a famous fan and a studio of their own. It also put them on Warner's roster in the same batch as Green Day, and the label's attention went where the sales did.

years.big: "Maybe tone it down on the verse a bit, Tom."
q: Totally surreal, but he was such a lovely fella.
years.src: The Quietus · Seb Chan · Louder Than War
years.h: Tom Jones covers A Girl Like You with the band backing him
years.p: Allen and Gray play bass and guitar on Jones's version for The Lead and How to Swing It, and write him Show Me (Some Devotion). Allen directed the vocal.
years.xp:
It started with Jones's label asking 4AD for material. "When we first heard about it we all burst out laughing," Allen told Seb Chan in 1995. Jones's answer to the direction, as Allen tells it: "Oh, OK then, right you are."

Thirty years on Allen still called it "totally surreal, but he was such a lovely fella."

years.src: Seb Chan · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Tom Jones walks on at 4AD's Los Angeles anniversary show
years.p: At All Virgos Are Mad, 4AD's 1995 concert series, Jones joins the band on stage.

years.src: Seb Chan · The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Two years in their own studio for Funky Little Demons
years.p: Hit money bought a studio, and no clock meant endless reworking. The album spends one week on the UK chart, at No. 75; Going South reaches No. 33 on the US alternative chart.
years.xp: "When you are paying for time in a studio you can't do that so you make do," Allen said at the time. Looking back, he and Gray are harder on it: Gray told the Quietus it was "bitty and lacked atmosphere," and Allen said they were exhausted and not communicating.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press · The Quietus
years.h: Mark Cox leaves just before the album comes out
years.p: Allen and Gray tour America as a duo. Gray told the Quietus that Cox hadn't really been coming in during the sessions, which made everything very hard.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Dropped before Christianity can come out
years.p: A video for Christianity is made and promo CDs go out in the US, then the band loses its deal. Gray: Warner had lost interest once Green Day took off, and Ivo had left 4AD.
years.xp:
"Ivo had left 4AD as well so we didn't have anyone in our camp there anymore, so that was kind of it really," Gray told the Quietus. Wikipedia says 4AD did the dropping; Gray names Warners.

Allen and Gray wrote a follow-up through 1995 and 1996, then conceded the band had run its course.

eras.title: Starting with the noise again
eras.text: Allen and Gray never stopped working together: Gray produced Allen's band Geniuser, and the lost mid-'90s demos finally surfaced on Record Store Day. Then, almost thirty years after the split, a new record with a new Gray.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Everything Is Beautiful sums it up, minus the debut
years.p: 4AD's retrospective is subtitled 1983–1995 but includes nothing from before 1984.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Gray produces Allen's band Geniuser
years.p: Allen fronts Geniuser with Giuseppe De Bellis, whom he calls the driving force; Gray produces the debut, Mud Black. Gray had already put out his own album as Limehouse Outlaw.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: The lost follow-up surfaces on Record Store Day
years.p: Unremembered Remembered collects six songs Allen and Gray cut in 1995 and 1996, billed as the band's last studio record. A seventh track stayed in the vault.

years.cap: Michael Allen, Andrew Gray and Stephen Gray, 2024
years.src: The Quietus · Louder Than War
years.h: Andrew Gray's brother Stephen takes Cox's seat for A 2nd Shape
years.p: Recorded on analogue gear, the album goes back to the noisy Burden of Mules sound. Stephen does what Cox once did: embellish what Allen and Andrew write.
years.xp:
"We always started with the noise," Allen told the Quietus, "and that's what we did with A 2nd Shape." Gray had given up on computers: "there's no headroom."

At a sold-out London show at the Lexington, Andrew Gray summed up the comeback for Louder Than War: "This morning I was hoovering my carpet, tonight I'm on stage in front of 200 people."

years.cap: The Wolfgang Press at the Lexington, London, January 11 2026
years.src: Louder Than War · Wikipedia: The Wolfgang Press
years.h: Asylum Variations, the second album in 18 months
years.p: The title nods to Elgar's Enigma Variations. Allen: a scary time, but "not a political album, as such."
